pos.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. Ferguson's 1995/96 side dominated at Old Trafford but did its damage with quick transitions through Giggs, Cole and Cantona rather than through sterile possession, which fits the 4-4-2-family context (Wilson, unverified).

pro.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. The team moved the ball forward quickly, with Schmeichel's fast distribution, Keane driving from midfield and rapid counters, and did not insist on playing out short under pressure.

est.personaBrief: There is no season-wide verified source. Context points to a 4-4-2 family shape (Wilson, unverified), and the opening day had Scholes playing off McClair (SI). By general knowledge it was a flat 4-4-2 with wingers holding the width, while Cantona roamed and dropped between the lines.

lar.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. Giggs on the left and Beckham or Sharpe on the right made wide play and crossing the team's main attacking route within the 4-4-2 context.

blo.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. The team was energetic in a mid-block 4-4-2 and worked to deny opponents time, but it regrouped into shape after losing the ball rather than counter-pressing systematically.

mar.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. The back four of Bruce and Pallister with the Nevilles or Irwin defended zonally in open play, while set pieces followed the English man-marking habits of the time, with no dedicated man-markers on stars.

pla.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. In the league Ferguson imposed his own attacking, front-foot identity on opponents. He adjusted personnel and details rather than his style, and the squad rebuild shows his idea being imposed on the club (Premier League review).

res.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. The side played attacking football, but Ferguson was relentlessly results-driven: it chased the title to a four-point margin (Premier League review) and won the FA Cup final 1-0, and he would protect late leads.

sis.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. Cantona and Giggs got creative licence within a disciplined collective in which everyone worked. Ferguson trusted his players' quality more than any system to make ordinary players great.

jog.personaBrief: Gap axis, so this comes from general knowledge. In mid-90s English football Ferguson valued intensity, pace and combativeness, with Keane, Butt, Cole and Giggs, while still building around Cantona, a technical playmaker who ran comparatively little.

bas.personaBrief: This is the verified core of the file. Ferguson sold Ince, Kanchelskis and Hughes, made no major signings and made Beckham, Scholes, the Nevilles and Butt regular starters (Premier League review, Wikipedia), starting four players aged 20 or under on opening day (SI). He won the title with the kids, against Hansen's line, though alongside veterans such as Bruce, Keane and Schmeichel.

lid.personaBrief: Ferguson used Hansen's remark to motivate the squad all season (Goal, paraphrase), and selling established stars shows his authority over the dressing room (Premier League review). By general knowledge he ran it firmly, with clear discipline and the final word on every decision.
